svg.title: Koḥlit, entries 11 and 60: every variant of a qualifying site
svg.text: Every variant of a qualifying “Koḥlit” — entries 11 and 60
Schematic plans, north up. Each panel is one reading or rule choice. Rings are to scale (1 km, dotted 0.5 km); features are enlarged.
Not reconstructions of any real site.

Not counted: the count assumes one site
Koḥlit (settlement; bearings from its centre point)
pool (C1); red × = “northern corner, dig four cubits” (recorded, not a condition)
side entrance facing north (Milik). A vertical shaft has no facing.
opening hidden under cover or fill (Puech)
grave or tomb; dashed circle = within 10 m of the opening
• Milik and Puech openings are recorded but not required, so V1 = V3, V2 = V4,
V5 = V7 and V6 = V8 in the count. They differ only in what to look for on the ground.
• Headline: the loose graves rule; the strict rule is reported beside it.
• Pool inside or outside the site both pass C1.
• Same everywhere: 90° quarters, ≤1 km (sensitivity runs at 0.5 and 2 km), features
dated to 135 CE or earlier or undated, and survey silence = unknown.
Entry 11 (II 13–15): “In the pool that is east of Koḥlit, in the northern corner, dig four
cubits: 22 talents.” Entry 60 (XII 10–13): “In the pit that is on the north side of Koḥlit,
its opening to the north, with tombs at its mouth: a copy of this document …”
